muc.title: What is machine learning?
muc.text: Your inbox knows which emails are spam on its own. Who taught it?

muc.title: Writing rules by hand
muc.text: The old way was writing rules by hand: if an email says "you won", it's spam. But spammers just change the wording and get through.

muc.title: Give the machine lots of examples
muc.text: Machine learning works differently. Instead of writing rules, you give the machine thousands of labeled examples: this is spam, this is a normal email.

muc.title: The machine finds the patterns
muc.text: The machine finds the signs by itself: lots of exclamation marks, unknown senders, pushing you to click a link. Nobody had to write those rules.

muc.title: Machine learning is everywhere
muc.text: Your phone recognizing your face, voice assistants understanding you, apps suggesting movies: all of them learn from examples like this.

muc.title: You can teach AI with examples too
muc.text: Chatbots work the same way. Instead of explaining at length what you want, give it a few examples.

muc.title: Give examples, ask for more
muc.text: Paste two or three examples you like, then type "write more in exactly this style". The result will be much closer to what you want.
